description: A short brief on one subject — a person, a firm, a publication — written from what is on the record and returned as text plus a link to a formatted page you can share. Say who the subject is and what kind of subject they are, because the brief is written for the kind: what matters about a founder is not what matters about a doctor. What comes back is about a page: who they are, what the record shows, what stands out, and what to be careful of. Ask for the same subject twice and the second time is free — you are handed the brief already written, unchanged, rather than paying for it again. Nothing is charged when there is no such subject or too little on the record to say anything useful. Subject types you can ask for, and what each costs: company (5 credits), counterparty (5 credits), crypto_coin (5 credits), donor (5 credits), executive (5 credits), expert_witness (5 credits), founder (5 credits), insurance_underwriting (5 credits), investor (5 credits), journalism_person (5 credits), journalist (5 credits), litigation_funder (5 credits), nft_collection (5 credits), pe_firm (5 credits), penny_stock (5 credits), physician (10 credits), pre_ipo_secondary (5 credits), publication (5 credits), source (5 credits), spac_sponsor (5 credits), specific_fund (5 credits), vc_firm (5 credits), wealth_advisor (5 credits). Use this when someone says "who is this", "what should I know before I meet them", "quick read on this firm". For the long version, use get_full_report.

company.description: Optional. The organisation they are with, or the domain, when the name on its own could mean several people.

new_report.description: Set this only when you want a fresh brief on a subject you already have one for. It writes and charges for a second brief and leaves the earlier one untouched. Leaving it off hands you the brief you already bought, free.

subject.description: Who or what the brief is about — a person's name, a firm, a publication. Add the employer or domain to it if the name alone is common.

subject_type.description: Which kind of subject this is. The accepted values are listed in this tool's description, each with its price; they are read from the live price list, so ask for one of those exactly.

name: get_snapshot

already_bought.description: True when this is one you already had, handed back free.

candidates.description: Companies the name could mean, each with its website and a line on what it does.

credits_charged.description: Credits this call took. 0 when nothing was charged.

did_you_mean.description: The closest accepted subject type, when the one given was not accepted.

error.description: Present when the call could not do the work; says why and that nothing was charged where that is so.

made_at.description: When it was written (ISO date and time). It is never edited afterwards.

message.description: A plain note about the answer, for example why candidates were returned instead of a result.

needs_website.description: True when several companies share the name; call again with the website in company.

note.description: A short note about this answer.

pricing_note.description: What this call cost and what a repeat costs.

public_url.description: A link to the formatted page you can share.

report.description: The written brief or report: text, or sections with their sources.

still_writing.description: True when a long report is still being written; come back to public_url.

subject.description: Who or what the brief or report is about.

subject_type.description: The kind of subject it was written for.

subject_types.description: The subject types that can be asked for, when the one given was not one of them.

upgrade_url.description: Where to see plans, when the subject type needs a plan the account does not have.

title: Short brief on one subject
